edition.alertText: Oil crashes 7.6% as draft Iran peace deal circulates after 3 days of Doha talks; Brent plunges to $104.77 — biggest single-day drop since July; WTI falls below $100 to $96.46; Iran condenses 7-step plan to 2-day Hormuz reopening; Iranian negotiators leave Doha — draft proposal circulating among mediators; Khamenei grants government 'powers' to accelerate talks; Trump: 'no rush' on strikes but warns of giving Iran 'the hammer'; US midterm elections today; Netanyahu pushed for post-midterm strikes — Trump reportedly rebuffed; Late Nov 1: tanker hit by 2 projectiles off Ras Al Khafji; Houthis claim 2 drones targeted KFIA Dammam airport — US Embassy reports delays; Saudi intercepts missile and drones; Houthis advance within 80 km of Aden; IMO: 123+ ships attacked since war began, likely more unreported; ~490 vessels waiting outside Hormuz; Goldman Sachs raises Dec Brent forecast to $105; US gasoline $4.17/gal

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis reached day 249 — US midterm election day — with the strongest diplomatic signals since the June Islamabad Memorandum colliding with Trump's barely veiled threats of post-election escalation. Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday after three consecutive days of Qatar-mediated talks, and a draft proposal for a US-Iran deal began circulating among mediators and regional capitals. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the seven-step plan first tabled at the UN General Assembly in September has been 'condensed and can be implemented within two days' — the first step requiring the US to lift its naval blockade and freeze sanctions, the second seeing Iran reopen the strait and resume talks on the nuclear programme. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei granted the government 'powers' to accelerate negotiations, per President Pezeshkian. Foreign Minister Araghchi, speaking in Ashgabat, said 'by accepting these conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened and negotiations will resume,' but warned Iran 'will not bow down' if rebuffed. Trump said there is 'no rush' to resume strikes, but at rallies in Iowa and Kansas warned he may have to give Tehran 'the hammer,' adding the war would end 'very soon, one way or the other.' Per Axios and Israel's Channel 12, Trump rebuffed Netanyahu's push to resume attacks immediately after the midterms, favoring continued talks. ABC News reported the US and Israel are nonetheless drawing up plans for post-election strikes. Ambassador Tom Barrack hinted 'dramatic steps' could come within two weeks.

Oil prices suffered their biggest single-day crash since July on Monday November 2, as the draft peace proposal raised hopes of a Hormuz reopening. Brent plunged 7.63% to $104.77 from its October 30 peak of $117.64, while WTI fell 7.36% to $96.46 — dropping below $100 for the first time since mid-October. By Tuesday morning, both benchmarks partially recovered: Brent traded at $105.38 (+0.59%) and WTI at $97.01 (+0.57%) as markets awaited midterm results that could reshape the war calculus. Goldman Sachs raised its December Brent forecast to $105, noting that peace hopes and war risks roughly offset. The 10-year Treasury yield fell below 4.87%, its lowest since September, as bond markets priced in easing energy inflation. Despite the crash, Brent remains roughly 60% above pre-war levels and has gained over 70% year-over-year. Gold traded at $3,952/oz (+0.14%), easing from safe-haven peaks as diplomatic optimism tempered demand. US gasoline averaged $4.17/gal (AAA), down 12 cents week-over-week but still 37% above a year ago. Diesel hit $6.29/gal. Saudi crude exports averaged 5.52M b/d in October (Kpler), but Ras Tanura loadings fell sharply from 4.16M b/d in September to 2.95M b/d as Gulf-side loading risks mount — Yanbu loadings also slipped from 2.54M to 2.21M b/d.

The maritime front saw a notable quiet spell over November 2–3, likely reflecting the diplomatic thaw, though the underlying threat remained severe. The late November 1 attacks — a tanker struck by two projectiles about 72 nautical miles east of Ras Al Khafji and a UKMTO-reported mine strike near Qeshm Island — brought the estimated wartime total to roughly 198 incidents. IMO said at least 123 ships have been confirmed attacked since February but cautioned the real number is likely higher, as vessels with false flags or fraudulent registries tend not to report. UKMTO logged 30+ attacks in October alone — double September and the worst month since the war began. An estimated 350–400 ships remain stranded in the Arabian Gulf, with approximately 490 vessels waiting outside the strait. On the Yemen front, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed two drones targeted King Fahd International Airport (KFIA) in Dammam over 48 hours; the US Embassy confirmed KFIA was 'operational with some delays and cancellations.' Saudi air defenses intercepted two drones over Riyadh and a Houthi ballistic missile in the south. The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi missile and drone sites in Dhamar and Hudaydah. Critically, Houthi ground forces advanced to within 80 km of Aden, the interim capital — their closest approach since 2015. VLCC spot rates eased further from their peaks as peace talk optimism dampened the war premium, with Clarksons eco-scrubber units at $541K/day and Gulf-Oman to China fixtures at $657K/day (Braemar), both down roughly 25% from the October highs.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%. Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for second consecutive month — September and October both zero (World Visualized/Syz Group tracking data). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. India building two fertiliser futures — diversifying sources while lobbying for corridor (Diplomat Magazine). Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Edison: 3 more cargoes cancelled for Italy. Dutch TTF gas surges to €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Europe and Asia face short-term supply heading into winter. Kpler: Asian LNG prices to rise amid simmering geopolitical tensions.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge.
